docs.title: Vision-Guided 3-Axis Pick-and-Place
docs.text:
A three-axis robotic manipulator that finds objects with a camera and picks and places them on its own, with real-time motor control in embedded C on a PSoC 5LP.

PSoC 5LPEmbedded COpenCVPIDMotor control

docs.title: System design
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  CAM[Camera] --> CV[OpenCV object localization]
  CV --> PID[Closed-loop PID correction]
  PID -->|setpoints| PSOC[PSoC 5LP<br/>embedded C motor control]
  PSOC --> DRV[Motor drivers]
  DRV --> ARM[3-axis manipulator + gripper]
  ARM -. position feedback .-> PID
Layer What I did Vision Object localization in OpenCV to find each target in the workspace Control Closed-loop PID correction that compensates positioning error while grasping Embedded Real-time motor control written in embedded C on the PSoC 5LP Hardware Integrated motor drivers, sensors and control hardware; board-level bring-up and I/O validation Verification End-to-end system tests over the full workspace

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
80 autonomous pick-and-place trials across a 350 × 200 × 150 mm workspace:

Metric Result Successful picks 74 / 80 (92.5%) Positioning accuracy ±2.5 mm Repeatability ±1.0 mm Mean cycle time 4.8 s per pick-and-place

Repeatability is tighter than accuracy, which points to a systematic offset rather than random error: the arm lands in the same place each time, a little away from the target. That makes camera-to-arm calibration the clearest next improvement.
